purpose: Notation Systems builds and operates provenance-bearing computational corpora. This file is the one declaration of what 'provenance' means across them, so that two corpora can disagree about a value without disagreeing about what a value's evidence claim IS.
why_this_exists: Measured, 2026-08-31: two repositories had independently built a lattice, both called it the evidence class, and neither knew the other existed.
data-acquisition-fabric (Python) fixes a class AT INGEST: asserted | computed | derived | measured. It answers HOW THE VALUE CAME TO EXIST.
Payload Terminal (TypeScript) carries a ranked class on every claim: reported | estimated | representative | derived. It answers HOW HARD THE EVIDENCE IS.

Those are two different questions, and the TypeScript module says so in its own header — 'Provenance answers where a number came from; source class answers how hard the evidence is' — and then implements only the second.

Neither repository is wrong. Each built one axis of a two-axis property and named it after the whole. This file names both axes so that a corpus can be missing one deliberately rather than by not having noticed.

production_class.question: How did this value come to exist?
production_class.ordering_note: NOT ranked. A measured value is not automatically better evidence than an asserted one — a mislabelled instrument beats an honest statement, and the ranking question belongs to claim_strength. Anyone who ranks these is answering a different axis's question with this axis's terms.
production_class.absence_note: `unclassified` is not a fifth term. It is the absence of one, and it is inadmissible for canonical assertion. It is never defaulted to any term.

claim_strength.question: How hard is the evidence for this claim about the world?
claim_strength.ordering_note: Higher is harder. The order is the CONTAMINATION direction, used when inputs combine.
claim_strength.absence_note: This axis has no declared absence term. A value with no claim_strength is not admissible; there is nothing to default it to. Adding an absence term here is a contract change, not an implementation detail.

interest.question: What stake did the source have in stating it this way?
interest.ordering_note: `unknown` sits ABOVE self_reported deliberately: not established is not the same as established to be interested. It is never collapsed into `disinterested`, which is how an interested number gets treated as a measurement.
interest.absence_note: Here the absence IS a term, and it is ranked, because an unestablished stake still has to combine with other inputs rather than halt them.

combination.statement: When a value is computed from several inputs, it takes the WEAKEST rank of any input on each ordered axis independently. A derived quantity is only as sound as its softest input.
combination.does_not_apply_note: production_class is unordered, so there is no weakest. A value computed from inputs of any production class is `computed` or `derived` by its own construction, not by the minimum of anything.
combination.opposite_direction_warning: The reverse rule — one good witness is enough — is correct for ENTITY EXISTENCE and wrong for quantities. Payload Terminal implements it separately as `strongestAttestingClass`. The two must never be unified; a contract that had one rule for both would silently launder a weak quantity through a well-attested subject.

contested_terms.note: Terms that appear on more than one axis. These are where a value crossing a corpus boundary can be corrupted while every local check passes, so each one is resolved here explicitly — including the ones resolved as REFUSED.

appears_in.claim_strength: the HARDEST class, rank 3 — a figure the source itself published.
appears_in.production_class_vocabulary_map: data-acquisition-fabric maps the presentation term `reported` onto `asserted`, its class for a party stating something.

reported.refusal_reason: The two uses point opposite ways. In claim_strength, `reported` is the strongest thing a value can be. In the production vocabulary it maps to `asserted`, which is the class you would trust LESS than `measured` because no instrument stands behind it. A value crossing from an acquisition corpus as `asserted` and arriving as `reported` would be promoted from 'a party claimed this' to 'hardest available evidence' by nothing but a shared spelling.
reported.what_a_caller_must_do: State claim_strength explicitly at the boundary from evidence about the SOURCE, not by translating the production class. There is no automatic mapping and this contract does not provide one.

appears_in.production_class: a value computed from other evidence.

derived.direction_reason: This one is sound in exactly one direction. A value whose PRODUCTION was derivation cannot have claim strength above `derived`, because it is downstream of inputs it did not measure. The converse does not hold: a value can carry claim_strength `derived` — because one of its inputs was representative — while its own production was a direct measurement.
derived.what_a_caller_must_do: Applying it backwards would relabel a measurement as a derivation on the strength of a weak input, which is a claim about how the number was made, and false.

data-acquisition-fabric.absence_note: An acquisition fabric records how a value was obtained. It is not the layer that decides how much a claim about the world is worth, and inventing a strength at ingest would be fabricating an assessment nobody made.

payload-terminal.absence_note: OPEN GAP, recorded rather than closed by assertion. Payload Terminal cannot today say whether a figure was measured or asserted upstream; it knows only how hard it judges the resulting claim. When an acquisition corpus feeds it, the production class arrives with the value and this becomes implementable.

what_conformance_proves: That each corpus's local vocabulary matches the terms this file declares for the axes it says it implements.
That the copy of this file each corpus carries hashes to the digest that corpus pins.

It does NOT prove the two copies are the same file. Each side verifies its own copy against its own pin; two equally stale copies pass every check either side has. Byte identity across corpora is coverage for divergence, not currency — the same limit the archive mirror states about itself, and it is stated here rather than left to be discovered.
